dedupe_keys.name: the vibration sensor on railway lines

description: The vibration sensor on railway lines is a data set deposited in University of Pretoria by its authors Motlalepule Machitje. This dataset is about using vibration sensing as a preventative maintenance strategy on the railway lines. Railway lines are suspectable to faults because of continuous movement of train on the track. These faults on track increase vibration frequencies on the track and if not corrected they will lead to catastrophic failures. Coverage: not stated; the metadata date the deposit to 2024. The formats are not stated in the metadata. Size stated: 8044604 Bytes. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet for this repository.
